author: Navjot Tomer (Mindstellar)
description_html:
Google Analytics

Adds Google Analytics 4 to the public side of your site, with consent gating and a per-browser opt-out.

Requirements

  • Shopclass 6.1.0 or later
  • PHP 8.0 or later
  • A Google Analytics 4 measurement ID

Install

  1. Open Plugins → Browse (or upload the zip from the GitHub release).
  2. Install.
  3. Activate.

If core already had a tracking ID (6.1.0 or earlier), install picks it up. No retyping.

Set up

  1. Open Plugins → Manage plugins, then Settings next to Google Analytics.
  2. Enter the Measurement ID. It must start with G-, GT-, UA- or AW-. Anything else is refused.
  3. Choose the switches: "Wait for consent before tracking" and "Ask Google to truncate visitor IP addresses".
  4. Save.

How it works

  • Consent Mode starts with storage denied, before the library loads. gtag.js sets no cookie or identifier until consent is granted.
  • Whatever asks the visitor calls oscGoogleAnalytics.grant() or oscGoogleAnalytics.deny(). Remembering the answer is the banner's job.
  • Turn the consent switch off if another tool already manages consent for the page.
  • The button "Stop counting this browser" marks this browser as not counted. Use it in each browser you visit from.
  • It loads on the public side only, never in the admin. It works with a page cache.

For developers

Filter google_analytics_should_track: return false to skip the tag for a request.

Support

https://github.com/mindstellar/shopclass-plugins/issues

License

GPL-3.0-or-later.

versions.changelog_html:
First release. Restores, as a plugin, the analytics core carried until 6.2.0 — and adds what a plain snippet does not.

New

  • Google Analytics 4 through gtag.js, configured from the admin.
  • Consent Mode, initialised denied before the library loads, with oscGoogleAnalytics.grant() / .deny() for a banner to call. Ordering matters: a default written after gtag.js has started arrives too late, and the first page view is already recorded with storage allowed.
  • A per-browser opt-out, set from the settings screen, so your own visits stay out of the numbers. Per-browser because an admin session cannot be seen from the public side of the site — and because deciding it in the browser leaves the page cacheable.
  • The tracking ID core used to hold is adopted on install, so an upgraded site keeps working without retyping it.
  • google_analytics_should_track filter for suppressing the tag per request.

Notes

  • The measurement ID is checked against the shapes Google issues before it is written into a page.
  • Output does not vary between tracked visitors, so the response cache is unaffected.
